documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 45 yo M.

Interval: dry cough on and off since around April. No fever, no sputum, no blood, no wheeze or chest tightness. Had a cold going around the house in the spring and thinks it started then. Some throat clearing in the mornings. Never smoker, no vaping. No heartburn. No new meds (none at all). Energy fine.

Exam: well, not coughing during the visit. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles or wheeze. Heart RRR. Abd benign. Skin clear. No LAD.

A/P
1. Cough ~2 mo, nonsmoker, normal exam: most likely post-viral or postnasal drip. Watchful waiting; saline rinses. If still going past the 8-week mark or any fever/SOB/weight loss, let me know and we'll go further.
2. Chronic mild anemia: recheck CBC.
3. Prostate screening: discussed starting at 45 given higher risk in Black men; he wants a PSA. Ordered.
4. Colon cancer screening due now: GI referral for colonoscopy.
5. CMP, lipids, A1c.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.4, normocytic, a little lower than last year, still mild. PSA 0.8. A1c, lipids, CMP normal. Will keep trending. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center. Procedure date 2023-08-08.
Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening, age 45.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: Boston Bowel Prep Scale 8 (3/3/2).
Findings: cecum reached and confirmed by appendiceal orifice area and ileocecal valve; post-appendectomy appearance. Normal mucosa throughout the colon on withdrawal. No polyps.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat in 10 years.

orders.reason: Chronic dry cough, sister with pulmonary sarcoidosis

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his home office.

Cough still there, ~4 months now. Dry, worse talking for long stretches on calls. Saline rinses didn't change it. More tired than usual the last few weeks, he figured from the cough and work. No fever, sweats, hemoptysis, chest pain, SOB on stairs. No new pets or hobbies, no travel.

He brought up his sister, who has pulmonary sarcoidosis, and asked whether this could be the same.

Obs on video: speaking full sentences, occasional dry cough, no distress.

A/P: Chronic dry cough in a nonsmoker, now well past the post-viral window, with a sister who has sarcoid. Referring straight to pulmonology for evaluation and imaging rather than piecemeal here. He's fine with that. Call sooner for fever, blood, or breathing trouble.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Comparison: none. The hila are bilaterally full, compatible with hilar lymph node enlargement. Lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contour otherwise normal. Osseous structures intact.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Seen 2023-10-05.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Mr. Robinson, 45, for chronic cough.

He describes about six months of nonproductive cough with generalized fatigue. Over the last two weeks painful red bumps have come up on both shins. No fever, hemoptysis, chest pain or recent infection. He has never been told he had tuberculosis, recalls no fungal exposures (no caving, construction dust, birds) and has not traveled recently. Never smoker; social alcohol; works in IT. No medications. NKDA. Appendectomy as a teen. Family: his sister has pulmonary sarcoidosis; father with type 2 diabetes; mother with autoimmune thyroiditis.

Exam: vital signs normal. Several tender erythematous nodules over both anterior tibial surfaces. Faint crackles at both bases, no wheeze. No clubbing. No palpable peripheral adenopathy. Heart regular. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Data: hemoglobin 10.5, MCV 82. Chest radiograph today shows bilateral hilar fullness.

Impression: subacute cough with bilateral hilar adenopathy and lesions typical of erythema nodosum. Sarcoidosis is the leading consideration, particularly with his family history; lymphoma and granulomatous infection need to be excluded.

Plan: bronchoscopy with sampling of the hilar nodes, scheduled for 10/19. I'll write again once pathology is back.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

reports.text:
Specimen: bilateral hilar lymph nodes, transbronchial sampling.
Gross: multiple tan tissue fragments and core material, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: lymph node tissue containing multiple well-formed non-caseating epithelioid granulomas with scattered multinucleated giant cells. No necrosis. AFB and GMS stains negative for organisms. No malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: Hilar lymph nodes: non-caseating granulomatous inflammation; special stains negative for acid-fast bacilli and fungi. No malignancy.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy Procedure Note
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside hospital bronchoscopy suite, 2023-10-19.
Indication: bilateral hilar adenopathy.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation with topical lidocaine.
Airway inspection: normal to the subsegmental level bilaterally, no endobronchial lesions.
Sampling: transbronchial needle passes from right and left hilar nodes; rapid on-site evaluation showed lymphocytes and granulomas.
Complications: none. Discharged home same day.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic.

Dear Doctor,

The hilar node samples from Mr. Robinson's bronchoscopy on 10/19 show non-caseating granulomas, with stains negative for mycobacteria and fungi and no malignant cells. Together with the bilateral hilar adenopathy and erythema nodosum, this fits sarcoidosis.

I spoke with him by phone today. This presentation tends to settle on its own, so I am not starting treatment. We will watch the cough and skin and see him back in the spring, sooner if he worsens. He knows to call with breathing trouble.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after pulm workup. Bronch 10/19, nodes with non-caseating granulomas, stains neg -> sarcoidosis per pulm, observation only. He's relieved it isn't cancer.

Cough the same, maybe slightly less. Shin bumps fading, less tender. Tired. No fevers. Eyes fine, no redness or blurring.

Exam: shins with a few faint violaceous macules, no active tender nodules. Lungs: no crackles appreciated today. Heart RRR.

Hgb 10.5 on pulm's CBC, MCV 82, down from 11.4 in June. Known chronic mild normocytic anemia, iron and vitamins were normal last year.

A/P
1. Sarcoidosis, pulm following, no treatment. Pulm f/u in spring.
2. Chronic anemia, a bit lower. Recheck with physical; low threshold for repeat iron studies.
3. Flu + updated COVID today.

documents.title: Cough update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just a quick update for my file. The bumps on my legs are totally gone and the cough has calmed way down, maybe once or twice a day now. Still more tired than I'd like but I'll take it. Pulm appointment is next month.

documents.title: RE: Cough update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great to hear, thanks for letting me know. Keep the pulmonology visit. If the tiredness doesn't keep improving, bring it up at your physical and we'll take a look.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Seen 2024-03-21.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson returns for sarcoidosis. His cough is much less frequent and the erythema nodosum has cleared. Some ongoing tiredness. No dyspnea, chest pain or eye symptoms.

Exam: vitals normal, oxygen saturation normal on room air. Lungs clear today. Shins clear.

Assessment: sarcoidosis, improving on observation alone. No indication for therapy.

Plan: continue observation; he will contact us if the cough returns or breathing changes.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M annual.

Sarcoid: cough basically gone, pulm in March said improving, observation. Shins clear.

Main complaint is fatigue, going on since last fall. Gets through the workday but wiped by evening, naps on weekends which isn't like him. Sleep 7 h, no snoring per wife. Mood OK, PHQ-9 3. Weight down ~2 kg since last year, not trying. Appetite "fine, maybe a little less."

Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft. Skin: no rash, shins clear. Thyroid normal size. No LAD.

A/P
1. Fatigue: CBC, CMP, TSH (mother with thyroiditis), A1c. Could be anemia, could be lingering sarcoid. Recheck after labs.
2. Chronic mild anemia: trending.
3. Sarcoidosis: per pulm.
4. Prevention: colonoscopy 2023 normal, PSA 2023 normal, flu/COVID in fall.

RTC 1 yr, sooner if fatigue worsens.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jamal, thyroid, kidney, liver, electrolytes and sugar are all normal. Your hemoglobin is 11.0, similar to the past couple of years, so it doesn't fully explain how tired you've been. Some of this may be your body still settling after the sarcoidosis. Let's see how the summer goes; if you're not feeling better, or if the weight keeps coming off, book a visit and we'll dig further.

orders.reason: Fatigue, weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation; evaluate for adrenal insufficiency

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired and weak.

Fatigue now about a year and getting worse, not better as hoped. New over the summer: legs and arms feel weak, harder carrying groceries up the stairs. Weight down again without trying. Wife noticed his forearms and elbows have gotten darker over the past few months; he hadn't paid it attention. No fever, no cough to speak of, no abdominal pain, no vomiting.

Exam: tired-appearing. BP lower than his usual. Weight 78.5 (83 at baseline). Skin: darker pigmentation over forearms and elbows, more than sun-exposed elsewhere. No focal weakness on exam. Lungs clear. Heart RRR.

A/P: Progressive fatigue, weakness, weight loss, low-normal BP and new hyperpigmentation. Primary adrenal insufficiency has to be ruled out first. Urgent endocrinology referral, front desk to call for the soonest slot. CMP today.

Go to the ED for vomiting, fainting, confusion or severe abdominal pain. Discussed why.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Urgent endocrinology referral faxed with today's note. Endo office offered 9/30 at 9:15, earliest available; asked to be placed on cancellation list. Pt informed by phone and agreed.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP normal, sodium and potassium in range. Normal lytes don't exclude adrenal insufficiency. Keep the endo appt. Pt informed.

medications.sig: Take 1 and 1/2 tablets (15 mg) by mouth on waking
Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth in the early afternoon
Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning
Inject 100 mg intramuscularly once for adrenal crisis or inability to keep oral steroids down, then call 911

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2024-09-30.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the urgent referral of Mr. Robinson, 46, with sarcoidosis followed by pulmonology and no prior steroid exposure.

History: roughly a year of steadily worsening fatigue and generalized muscle weakness, unplanned weight loss, and several months of darkening over the forearms and elbows. No medications. NKDA.

Exam: BP 100/60, HR 82. Weight 78 kg. Increased pigmentation in the palmar creases and on the buccal mucosa. No goiter.

Labs: CBC with a mild normocytic anemia and eosinophils of 14%. A cosyntropin stimulation test done in our office showed only a very small rise in serum cortisol.

Impression: primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease).

Plan:
- Hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg in the early afternoon.
- Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg each morning.
- Hydrocortisone 100 mg IM emergency kit prescribed; injection technique taught.
- Sick-day rules: double oral doses for fever or significant illness, triple for high fever; injection and ED for vomiting.
- Medical alert ID recommended.
- Follow-up here in about 3 months.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u new dx primary adrenal insufficiency (endo 9/30). On hydrocortisone 15 mg AM / 5 mg early afternoon, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. Has the IM hydrocortisone kit at home, wife shown how to use it too.

One week in: "like someone turned the lights back on." Appetite better.

Exam: BP improved. Hyperpigmentation unchanged (expected to fade slowly).

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency: reviewed sick-day rules again, he can recite them. Med alert bracelet ordered online. Flagged in chart: stress-dose steroids for procedures/surgery. Endo f/u January.
2. Sarcoidosis: quiet.
3. Chronic anemia: recheck at physical.
4. Flu + COVID today.

documents.title: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: refill request hydrocortisone 10 mg and 5 mg tabs, 90-day supply requested for mail order. Original Rx from endocrinology. Called endo office, they prefer to keep prescribing; they sent 90-day Rxs today. Pharmacy and pt notified.
